tools.name: proxy
tools.description: Residential proxy for AI agents. Pay for gigabytes of traffic and get a proxy login (host, port, username, password) after payment, to use with curl, a browser or any HTTP client. Choose a country, rotate the IP on every connection or keep one with a session tag. A pack lasts 90 days. Pay per pack i

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch one URL from a residential IP and get the raw response as JSON: status, final URL, headers and body (text or base64), up to 10 MB. GET, HEAD or POST, your own headers, an optional country. No JavaScript rendering. You pay for the megabytes delivered; a fetch that fails is not charged. Pay per

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Free. Tell the people who run this service what worked, what failed or what you miss: a bug, an idea or a thanks. A person reads it. No payment, no account; limited to a few messages an hour.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "proxy" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Residential proxy for AI agents. Pay for gigabytes of traffic and get a proxy login (host, port, username, password) after payment, to use with curl, a browser …

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch · Private data: proxy · Public sink: fetch · Destructive: feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch · Private data: proxy · Public sink: fetch · Destructive: feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "proxy" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
